decks.module: Who Must Hold an Oklahoma License
decks.domain: How to Apply for Your Oklahoma Driver License

cards.front: Who must hold an Oklahoma driver license, and who may be exempt
cards.back: Every resident driving on Oklahoma roads needs an Oklahoma license, out-of-state licensees must apply once resident and register their vehicles too, and only military personnel with spouses may be exempt.

cards.front: What must newcomers with other-state licenses do, and who may stay exempt
cards.back: Newcomers holding other-state licenses must earn an Oklahoma card and plate their vehicles once resident, while military personnel with spouses may stay exempt.
cards.memory_hook: Newcomers card and plate, military exempt

cards.front: Which drivers need no Oklahoma license at all
cards.back: No state license is needed by licensed sixteen-plus nonresidents, active-duty military families on home licenses, enrolled nonresident college students with families on home licenses, or farm tractor and implement operators working purely on farms and ranches.

cards.front: Do out-of-state students and farm tractor operators need an Oklahoma license
cards.back: Out-of-state students ride on valid home-state licenses, while farm tractor and implement hands need no license at all for pure field work.
cards.memory_hook: Students ride home licenses, farmhands none

decks.domain: How to Apply for Your Oklahoma Driver License

cards.front: How do you apply in person, and which identity papers count
cards.back: Apply in person at a Service Oklahoma testing facility under your full legal name, show any marriage, court, or divorce name change exactly as the source certificate, order, or decree words it, and bring one original or certified primary ID such as a birth certificate, valid passport, Oklahoma card first issued after November first two thousand seven, naturalization paper, consular birth report, resident or work card, or foreign passport with visa and I ninety-four, since notarized copies and photocopies fail.
cards.memory_hook: Full legal name, one primary original

cards.front: Which identity papers do counters accept, and which always fail
cards.back: Counters take original or certified identity papers only, so notarized copies and photocopies always fail.

cards.front: What proof do a replacement card, a long-expired renewal, and a new name each need
cards.back: Replacing a lost, stolen, or damaged card needs a primary ID at minimum, renewing a card expired over a year needs one primary-list document, and taking a new name needs government proof like a passport, qualifying divorce or adoption or name-change decree, birth certificate, marriage license, notarized common-law affidavit plus another primary source, or USCIS name-change evidence when the primary ID is a USCIS paper.

cards.front: What must happen before a name update, and who gets no license
cards.back: Report legal name changes to Social Security before updating the card, leave titles and church names off entirely, and prove lawful presence as a non-citizen because visitors and residency-ineligible immigrants get nothing while application receipts prove nothing.

cards.front: Where must a name change be logged first, and do titles print on the card
cards.back: Log name changes with Social Security before seeking the card update, and never expect titles or church names to print.
cards.memory_hook: Log it first, titles never print

cards.front: Does an application receipt prove lawful presence, and who draws no license
cards.back: An application receipt never proves lawful presence, and visitors plus residency-ineligible immigrants draw no license.

cards.front: What else must you bring for the test, and what happens without driver education
cards.back: Bring insurance proof for the driving test, a doctor statement for impairing health conditions, your Social Security number which never prints, and a driver-education certificate from a public, commercial, or approved parent-taught course or risk added restrictions.

decks.domain: How to Apply for Your Oklahoma Driver License

cards.front: What is REAL ID, and what does it unlock from May twenty twenty-five
cards.back: REAL ID adds a federal security standard to state cards, and from May seventh twenty twenty-five only a REAL ID card or federal ID such as a passport boards domestic flights or enters military bases, named federal buildings, and nuclear plants.
cards.memory_hook: REAL ID flies and enters bases

cards.front: From what date do only REAL ID or federal IDs board flights and enter bases
cards.back: Starting May seventh twenty twenty-five, only REAL ID cards or federal IDs board domestic flights and enter military bases, named federal buildings, and nuclear plants.

cards.front: What do commercial Classes A, B, and C cover, and how does the commercial permit work
cards.back: Commercial Class A, B, or C at eighteen spans vehicles rated twenty-six thousand one pounds or more except farm rigs, placarded hazmat carriers, and sixteen-plus-seat passenger vehicles, needs commercial-manual study plus registry-listed entry-level training, while its learner permit adds full Class D exams plus all commercial tests but skills, English literacy, a twenty-one-plus rated companion, one hundred eighty days plus one renewal, skills eligibility after fourteen days, and three tries before monthly retakes.

cards.front: What does Class D cover at eighteen, and when can you take the road test
cards.back: Class D at eighteen covers cars, vans, light trucks, recreation vehicles, and fire trucks with no course required, tests thirty days after the permit beside a twenty-one-plus licensed companion or the next business day after the written exam, and allows three sittings before monthly retakes or a thirty-day permit hold after three failures.

cards.front: At eighteen, how do commercial and Class D course requirements differ
cards.back: Eighteen opens both commercial and Class D, but commercial rigs need manual study plus registry training while Class D needs no course at all.
cards.memory_hook: Commercial studies, Class D no course

cards.front: How do the commercial and Class D permit waits and retake caps compare
cards.back: Commercial permits wait fourteen days for skills while Class D permits wait thirty, both cap tries at three before monthly retakes, yet the written-to-road path tests next business day and then demands a thirty-day permit after three failures.

decks.domain: How to Apply for Your Oklahoma Driver License

cards.front: What do intermediate and learner permits require at fifteen, sixteen, and sixteen and a half
cards.back: Intermediate Class D at sixteen needs a driver-education certificate while sixteen-and-one-half needs none, both demand a one-hundred-eighty-day permit and a Work Zone Safe certificate with the restriction clearing after six months with schooling or a year without, and learner permits at fifteen need course enrollment or completion papers or a parent-taught affidavit with receipt while sixteen needs only Class D qualification minus the road test, all learner driving beside a twenty-one-plus licensee, testing after one hundred eighty days, and three tries before monthly retakes.
cards.memory_hook: Sixteen with schooling, learner at fifteen

cards.front: How do schooling and age trade off for intermediate timing and permits
cards.back: Sixteen with schooling beats sixteen-and-one-half without for intermediate timing, six-month restriction clearance beats a full year with schooling, and fifteen needs course papers where sixteen needs none for a learner permit.

cards.front: What is parent-taught driver education, and what hours does it demand
cards.back: Parent-taught driver education, lawful since November first two thousand one, sells approved correspondence courses to students beyond school or commercial reach, charges vendor fees, runs self-paced without shortcutting, and still demands thirty classroom plus fifty-five driving hours.

cards.front: What do parent-taught courses charge and demand
cards.back: Parent-taught courses charge vendor fees, pace to the student without shortcutting, and still require thirty classroom plus fifty-five driving hours.

cards.front: What hours, passenger cap, and penalties does the graduated law set for teens
cards.back: The graduated law phases teen freedom to five in the morning through ten at night driving except for work, school, worship, or a twenty-one-plus companion, caps outsider passengers at one under the same exception, freezes violators at their level six months past conviction, accepts any Service Oklahoma-certified course, and answers twenty-five percent of sixteen-year-olds crashing or ticketing in year one while all fifty states run graduated programs.

cards.front: How many outsider passengers may a teen carry, and what freezes their level
cards.back: Teens drive five in the morning through ten at night except for work, school, worship, or a twenty-one-plus companion, carry at most one outsider passenger under the same exception, and freeze at-level six months past a moving conviction.

decks.domain: How to Apply for Your Oklahoma Driver License

cards.front: How does a motorcycle endorsement differ from a motorcycle-only license at fourteen
cards.back: A motorcycle endorsement attaches to any license class with Motorcycle Safety Foundation course graduates possibly skipping both tests, while a motorcycle-only license at fourteen adds the motorcycle manual to vision, written, and skills exams, caps machines at three hundred cubic centimeters, permits only half past four in the morning until nine at night solo riding, lets mid-size bikes run posted limits except on minimum-speed highways, frees riders at sixteen, and since August twenty-sixth twenty sixteen requires a certified basic rider course under eighteen.

cards.front: How does an endorsement differ from starting motorcycle-only at fourteen
cards.back: Endorsements attach to a live license with course waivers possible, while motorcycle-only at fourteen starts from vision, written, skills, and the bike manual.
cards.memory_hook: Endorse a license, or start fresh

cards.front: When may young small-bike riders ride solo, and what course is required under eighteen
cards.back: Small-bike riders keep a half-past-four-to-nine solo window with mid-size posted-limit carve-outs until sixteen, plus a certified rider course under eighteen.
cards.memory_hook: Half past four to nine solo

cards.front: What does a motorcycle learner permit at fourteen require, and what do ID cards need
cards.back: A motorcycle learner permit at fourteen may also be waived by course proof, requires helmets under eighteen and watchful twenty-one-plus endorsed supervision, gains a number-nine restriction at sixteen or fifteen with schooling, clears after thirty days, needs a parent signature accepting liability at fourteen and fifteen, and identification cards meanwhile serve any age for identity only with residency, license-grade proof, an in-person visit, and under-eighteen parent consent.

cards.front: What does a motorcycle permit need to clear, and what does an ID card need
cards.back: Permits need watchful endorsed supervision, a number-nine restriction at sixteen or fifteen with schooling, thirty days to clear, and a liability-accepting parent signature at fourteen and fifteen, while ID cards need only residency, proof, a visit, and under-eighteen consent.

decks.domain: How to Apply for Your Oklahoma Driver License

cards.front: What three exams make up Class D, and when are fees paid
cards.back: Class D means three exams, vision, written, and driving, at a Service Oklahoma site with no testing fee, fees collected only after passing for a paper temporary ahead of the mailed plastic, and applicants must know a Social Security number that never prints on the card.

cards.front: Do the Class D exams cost anything, and what bridges to the plastic card
cards.back: All three Class D exams test free, money changes hands only after passing, and a paper temporary bridges to the mailed plastic.
cards.memory_hook: Free tests, paper temp, plastic mailed

cards.front: Where do written questions come from, and how soon can you retake
cards.back: Written questions come from this manual over traffic law, safe practice, and drug and alcohol rules plus local city ordinances, commercial and motorcycle seekers study supplements, oral sittings come on request, and failure idles you at least one full day.

cards.front: Can the written test be taken orally, and what follows a failure
cards.back: Written questions lift from this manual, oral sittings come on request, and failure idles retakes a full day.

cards.front: What must you bring to the road test, and what does it score
cards.back: The road test requires passed vision and written exams, a tagged roadworthy car with its security form and no pets or extra occupants, offers certified-instructor examiners for a fee since November first twenty twelve beside free Service Oklahoma sittings, scores control, turns, backing, hill and parallel parking, signals, lanes, signs, right-of-way, and hazard response along an examiner route, and cancels on slick or hazardous pavement.
cards.memory_hook: Tagged car, security form, no pets

cards.front: Who gives road tests, and what weather cancels them
cards.back: Certified instructors sell skills sittings while Service Oklahoma gives them free, and slick or hazardous pavement cancels every road test.
cards.memory_hook: Instructors charge, state free, slick cancels

cards.front: Which tests does the requirements table assign to each applicant type
cards.back: Table two marks vision, written, and driving required for new sixteen-plus drivers with under-eighteen cards probationary, vision plus written for fifteen-plus learners with driving gated to sixteen and a six-month permit, all three for sixteen-plus motorcyclists, vision plus written for fourteen- and fifteen-year-old riders with driving after a thirty-day permit, nothing for sub-three-year renewals bearing license and presence proof, all three past three lapsed years, vision only with the rest waivable for valid out-of-state Class D holders, and nothing for ID cards beyond license-grade proof.

cards.front: How do renewal lapses and out-of-state transfers change the tests required
cards.back: Learners and young riders gate driving on age plus permit tenure, renewals split at three lapsed years between nothing and everything, and valid out-of-state transfers keep vision while shedding the rest at examiner discretion.

decks.module: Road Test Results, Fees and Vehicle Checks
decks.domain: How to Apply for Your Oklahoma Driver License

cards.front: Why do road tests fail, and what does a donor yes mean
cards.back: Road tests fail for error counts, danger, violations, crashes, or refused maneuvers with faults explained and a retest date set, testing spans the state at Service Oklahoma and licensed-operator sites, and issuance offers donor registry signup where yes prints a red heart as legal recovery consent, family notice stays optional, and LifeShare of Oklahoma fields questions.

cards.front: What fails a road test, and how does a donor no work
cards.back: Error counts, danger, violations, crashes, and refusals fail road tests with faults explained and dates set, while donor yes binds as a red-heart consent and no simply opts out with family notice optional.

cards.front: How is the veteran logo earned, and when must relocating offenders register
cards.back: Senate Bill one thirty-eight honors veterans with a flag-and-Veteran card logo for military ID, DD two fourteen, DD two fifteen, honorable World War II discharge, VA photo ID, or Guard NGB Form twenty-two holders, free of logo charge though card fees apply, while relocating sex and violent offenders must register with Corrections inside ten days and local police inside three or face fine or jail.

cards.front: Does the veteran logo cost anything, and what are the offender deadlines
cards.back: Veteran logos cost nothing but demand service proof while card fees still apply, and relocating offenders face ten days for Corrections but three for local police.
cards.memory_hook: Logo free, ten and three days

cards.front: When must you show your license, and what does a Class D cost
cards.back: Memorize your license number, carry the card whenever driving, display it to troopers, officers, sheriffs, and judges on demand and to anyone you crash with, show primary ID for originals, retests, renewals, ID cards, and replacements, and under the June-first-twenty-twenty-five table a four-year Class D runs four dollars to apply plus thirty-eight dollars and fifty cents in license fees, forty-two dollars and fifty cents overall, four-dollar retests, twenty-five-dollar replacements, and zero charge past sixty-five, all payable at Service Oklahoma or a licensed operator after every exam passes.

cards.front: What duties come with carrying a license, and who pays nothing
cards.back: Carry and display duties pair with primary-ID proof for every card transaction, and the June table prices Class D at forty-two fifty while sixty-five-plus pays nothing.

cards.front: What equipment must a vehicle carry, and what does the pre-test checklist cover
cards.back: Every vehicle must carry chapter-twelve Title-forty-seven equipment for officer inspection under section thirteen-one hundred two, and the pre-test checklist wants a valid plate, working brake and signal lamps including the third brake light on cars since nineteen eighty-six and trucks since nineteen ninety-four with untaped lenses, sound glass with tint inside five inches and above the AS-one line, tires above two thirty-seconds tread with no cords or bulges, a two-hundred-foot horn, firm brakes, two-sided front handles, working belts, left-outside plus center-or-right mirrors, and a current insurance form covering the driver.

cards.front: What does the pre-test list check on your vehicle
cards.back: Chapter-twelve equipment faces section inspection, and the pre-test list checks plate, lamps with third-light years, glass and tint bounds, tire tread and shape, horn reach, brakes, handles, belts, mirrors, and driver-covering insurance.
